It’s not that flat oil benchmark prices crashed, perhaps more importantly the physical market sent an even stronger signal of the wave of supply. 

The physical premium in the Middle East market (Oman vs Dubai) plunged today to almost zero (from >$30 a barrel in mid Sept). In the Dated Brent market, the physical premium for North Sea crude plunged to minus ~$1 a barrel (it was plus ~$19 in early Oct). 

The physical premia in both the Middle East and North Sea markets is now the lowest in about 3 ½ months.

Vitol CEO warns that the oil market “correction could be quite severe” if the U.S. and Iran reach an agreement. 

(He’s not making a bet on the likelihood of a deal, but expressing a view on what would happen to oil on the day after if one was to happen)
Vitol CEO says that it would take a full year before global oil demand recovers to the 2025 level (so basically, if the crisis was to end now, 2028 consumption would reach 2025 level)

At the top Middle East oil conference, Biden administration energy adviser @AmosHochstein has a message to the Trump administration energy officials (who cancelled their trips to Abu Dhabi): “The least you can do is to show up.”

The Chinese view on the Strait of Hormuz keeps hardening (against Iran). This is the joint communique between China and Oman, issued today: 

“….The two sides believed that the Strait of Hormuz should return to normal and safely open to navigation…”

Prime Minister Mark Carney faces a wave of court challenges to his decision to fast-track a pipeline project under a legal mechanism his government devised to speed up construction of major infrastructure.

Nine Indigenous groups have requested that a judge review and overturn the Canadian government’s Oct. 1 order to designate a proposed crude oil pipeline from Alberta to the west coast as a “project of national interest” to accelerate its building.

The fresh claims filed Oct. 30 come from British Columbia communities including the Cheam First Nation, Boston Bar First Nation, Lower Nicola Indian Band, Kwantlen First Nation and Tsartlip First Nation, according to a Monday news release. #oott https://t.co/zCsJ9AeWyH
